title: Token Economics Explorer — pricing & attribution UX prototype
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: design a Token Economics Explorer in the Redwood Console that surfaces token-level cost breakdowns, attribution across routes/models/customers, and exportable reports. The view should help engineering and finance stakeholders answer: 
- Where are we spending tokens (routes, models, time windows)?
- How much does a given route or feature cost per user/tenant?
- Which model variants drive increased spend and where can customers apply quantization/batching recommendations?
Scope: interactive dashboard panel in Billing > Insights, a dedicated attribution modal, and a compact pricing patterns UI to suggest control levers. Deliverables: mid-fi Figma prototype, annotated spec for ENG including required telemetry, CSV/BigQuery export spec, acceptance criteria, and a short usability checklist for support reps.
comments: 2026-02-20: Kickoff sync — aligned with PM on primary user personas (FinOps, Platform, Product) and top questions to answer. Decided to prioritize per-route + per-model attribution over per-token source labeling for MVP due to data availability.
2026-02-26: Mid-fidelity demo — design presented heatmap + stacked bar breakdown. PM requested clearer CTA for exporting and a compact pricing pattern card to explain trade-offs (latency vs cost).

2026-03-03: ENG feasibility review — ENG asked for clarification on aggregation windows, cardinality limits, and whether we can compute attribution at write-time vs near-real-time. Action: provide fallback UI when attribution is delayed >24h.
2026-03-08: Accessibility pass — updated color palette and added patterns for screen-reader friendly table summaries. Contrast checks OK.
2026-03-12: Design review with finance partner — added per-tenant amortized cost column and export template for quarterly reporting. Finance requested sample data for export preview.
Next steps: finalize export spec, handoff to ENG with telemetry schema, and schedule a short usability test with two customers (internal finance + early adopter).
acceptance_criteria: Dashboard panel shows total token spend and percentage breakdown by route and model for a selectable time window (24h, 7d, 30d, custom).
Attribution modal links a selected bar segment to a list of top contributing requests with anonymized IDs and cost per request.
Export feature allows CSV and BigQuery-compatible JSON export with a documented schema and preview.
Pricing patterns UI surfaces three recommended levers (batching, quantization profile, route-level limits) with estimated cost impact and confidence scores.
Fallback state handles delayed attribution gracefully with a clear age indicator and last-updated timestamp.
Design handoff includes Figma prototype, component specs, microinteraction notes, and annotated telemetry fields required by ENG.
